meta.note: Events are written from cited sources and dated. Arrows from a capital mean an action by that country's government.

places.name: Tehran
places.why: Iran's capital and biggest city. The government and the Supreme Leader's office are here.

places.name: Isfahan
places.why: Big city in central Iran. A nuclear technology centre and uranium plant sit just outside it. The IAEA says it does not know the plant's status.

places.name: Tabriz
places.why: Biggest city in Iran's northwest, close to Turkey, Armenia and Azerbaijan.

places.name: Mashhad
places.why: Iran's second biggest city, in the far northeast near Turkmenistan and Afghanistan. A major religious centre.

places.name: Shiraz
places.why: Big city in the south. It has a major air base and sits on the road to the Gulf coast.

places.name: Qom
places.why: Religious city south of Tehran. The Fordow nuclear site is dug into a mountain nearby.

places.name: Bandar Abbas
places.why: Iran's main port and navy base, right on the Strait of Hormuz.

places.name: Bushehr nuclear power plant
places.why: Iran's only working nuclear power station, on the Persian Gulf coast. Built with Russian help.

places.name: Natanz
places.why: Iran's main uranium enrichment site, partly underground. Enrichment is the step that can lead to bomb fuel.

places.name: Fordow
places.why: Uranium enrichment site built deep inside a mountain near Qom. It was bombed in June 2025, and the IAEA has had no access since.

places.name: Arak reactor
places.why: Heavy water reactor site near Arak. This kind of reactor can make plutonium, another possible bomb fuel.

places.name: Parchin
places.why: Military complex southeast of Tehran, long linked to missile and explosives work.

places.name: Kharg Island
places.why: Small island in the Persian Gulf. Most of Iran's crude oil exports are loaded onto tankers here.
places.country_note: the island is too small to appear on the 1:50m country shapes

places.name: Chabahar
places.why: Iran's only ocean port, on the Gulf of Oman outside the Strait of Hormuz. India has invested in it.

places.name: Qeshm Island
places.why: Iran's biggest island, lying along the Strait of Hormuz. Iranian forces are based on it.

places.name: Strait of Hormuz
places.why: Narrow passage between Iran and Oman. A large share of the world's oil and gas normally passes through it.
places.country_note: a sea passage between two countries

places.name: Persian Gulf
places.why: The sea between Iran and the Arab Gulf states. Much of the world's oil is loaded onto tankers here.

places.name: Gulf of Oman
places.why: The sea just outside the Strait of Hormuz, leading to the Arabian Sea and the Indian Ocean.

places.name: Caspian Sea
places.why: The world's largest lake, north of Iran. Iran shares it with Russia, Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan and Azerbaijan.

places.name: Red Sea
places.why: Sea between Africa and Arabia. Ships use it to reach the Suez Canal, the short route between Asia and Europe.

places.name: Arabian Sea
places.why: Part of the Indian Ocean south of Iran and Pakistan. US Navy carriers often operate here.

places.name: Bab al-Mandab
places.why: Narrow passage at the south end of the Red Sea, next to Yemen. Ships heading for the Suez Canal must pass it.
places.country_note: a sea passage between two countries

places.name: Suez Canal
places.why: Man-made canal in Egypt that links the Red Sea and the Mediterranean, the short sea route between Asia and Europe.

places.name: Mediterranean Sea
places.why: The sea between Europe, North Africa and the Middle East.

places.name: Black Sea
places.why: Sea shared by Ukraine, Russia, Turkey and others. Ukraine exports grain across it.

places.name: Al Udeid Air Base
places.why: The biggest US air base in the Middle East and the forward headquarters of US Central Command.

places.name: US Fifth Fleet base
places.why: Home of the US Navy's Fifth Fleet, which patrols the Persian Gulf, the Red Sea and the Arabian Sea.
places.ref_note: Only OpenStreetMap has a coordinate for this place, so it has one reference.

places.name: Al Asad Air Base
places.why: Large air base in western Iraq that hosted US troops for years. Iraq took full control in January 2026, and the US-led coalition ended its mission in Iraq on 30 September.

places.name: Al Dhafra Air Base
places.why: Air base near Abu Dhabi used by US aircraft, across the Gulf from Iran.
places.osm: Al Dhafra Air Base, United Arab Emirates

places.name: Prince Sultan Air Base
places.why: Saudi air base south of Riyadh that hosts US aircraft and air defences.
places.osm: Prince Sultan Air Base, Saudi Arabia

places.name: Camp Arifjan
places.why: US Army base in Kuwait, a supply hub for US forces in the region.

places.name: Diego Garcia
places.why: Remote island base in the Indian Ocean used by US long-range bombers.
places.country_note: a remote island not drawn on the country shapes

places.name: Jerusalem
places.why: Seat of Israel's government. Its status is disputed, and Palestinians want East Jerusalem as their capital.

places.name: Tel Aviv
places.why: Israel's business centre and home of its military headquarters. Most foreign embassies are here.

places.name: Gaza City
places.why: Biggest city in the Gaza Strip. A ceasefire between Israel and Hamas was announced in October 2025, but Israeli strikes continue.

places.name: Rafah
places.why: City at the south end of Gaza, on the border with Egypt.
places.ref_note: OpenStreetMap search returned nothing for this name; Wikipedia is the one reference.

places.name: Beirut
places.why: Lebanon's capital. Hezbollah, an armed group and party backed by Iran, is strong in its southern suburbs.

places.name: Bekaa Valley
places.why: Eastern Lebanon, along the Syrian border. A Hezbollah stronghold and supply route.

places.name: Damascus
places.why: Syria's capital. A new government took over after President Assad fell in December 2024.

places.name: Baghdad
places.why: Iraq's capital. Iraq's government balances between the US and Iran, and Iran-backed militias are strong here.

places.name: Jurf al-Sakhar
places.why: Town south of Baghdad controlled by Kataib Hezbollah, an Iran-backed militia.

places.name: Sanaa
places.why: Yemen's capital, held by the Houthis, an armed movement backed by Iran.

places.name: Riyadh
places.why: Capital of Saudi Arabia, the biggest Arab oil exporter and Iran's main rival across the Gulf.

places.name: Yanbu
places.why: Saudi oil port on the Red Sea. It lets Saudi Arabia export oil without using the Strait of Hormuz.

places.name: Doha
places.why: Capital of Qatar, a small gas-rich state that often carries messages between the US and Iran.

places.name: Manama
places.why: Capital of Bahrain, a small island state that hosts the US Navy's Fifth Fleet.

places.name: Abu Dhabi
places.why: Capital of the United Arab Emirates, a rich Gulf state across the water from Iran.

places.name: Kuwait City
places.why: Capital of Kuwait, a small oil state at the top of the Persian Gulf between Iraq and Saudi Arabia.

places.name: Muscat
places.why: Capital of Oman, which shares the Strait of Hormuz with Iran and has often hosted quiet US and Iran talks.

places.name: Islamabad
places.why: Capital of Pakistan, Iran's eastern neighbour and a nuclear-armed state.

places.name: Kabul
places.why: Capital of Afghanistan, ruled by the Taliban since 2021.

places.name: Ankara
places.why: Capital of Turkey, a NATO member that borders Iran, Iraq and Syria.

places.name: Cairo
places.why: Capital of Egypt, which borders Gaza and runs the Suez Canal.

places.name: Washington, D.C.
places.why: Capital of the United States. Arrows from here mean a decision or action by the US government.

places.name: Corpus Christi
places.why: Oil port on the Texas coast.

places.name: Caracas
places.why: Capital of Venezuela, which has the world's largest known oil reserves.

places.name: Moscow
places.why: Capital of Russia.

places.name: Kyiv
places.why: Capital of Ukraine, which Russia invaded in February 2022.

places.name: Crimean Bridge
places.why: Bridge over the Kerch Strait that links Russia to Crimea, the Ukrainian peninsula Russia seized in 2014.
places.ref_note: Only OpenStreetMap has a coordinate for this place, so it has one reference.
places.country_note: a bridge over water between Russia and occupied Crimea

places.name: Vienna
places.why: Capital of Austria and home of the IAEA, the UN agency that inspects nuclear sites.

places.name: London
places.why: Capital of the United Kingdom.

places.name: Beijing
places.why: Capital of China. Arrows from here mean a decision or action by China's government.

places.name: Hong Kong
places.why: A special administrative region of China on its south coast and a major hub for finance and trade.

places.name: Taipei
places.why: Capital of Taiwan, a self-governed island that China claims as its own territory.

places.name: Taiwan Strait
places.why: The sea between China and Taiwan, about 130 to 180 km wide, and a busy shipping route.

places.name: Tokyo
places.why: Capital of Japan, a US ally.

places.name: Seoul
places.why: Capital of South Korea, a US ally, only about 50 km from the North Korean border.

places.name: Pyongyang
places.why: Capital of North Korea, which has nuclear weapons and tests missiles often.

places.name: Sea of Japan (East Sea)
places.why: The sea between Japan and the Korean peninsula. Korea calls it the East Sea. North Korean test missiles often land here.

places.name: Manila
places.why: Capital of the Philippines, a US treaty ally.

places.name: Scarborough Shoal
places.why: Ring of reefs in the South China Sea claimed by both China and the Philippines. China has controlled it since 2012.
places.country_note: a disputed reef in open sea

places.name: South China Sea
places.why: Sea between China, Vietnam, the Philippines and Malaysia. China claims most of it, and about a third of world shipping crosses it.

places.name: Jakarta
places.why: Capital of Indonesia.

places.name: New Delhi
places.why: Capital of India.

places.name: Khartoum
places.why: Sudan's capital, where the civil war began in April 2023.

places.name: Port Sudan
places.why: Red Sea port that became the base of Sudan's army-led government during the war.

places.name: El Obeid
places.why: Main city of Sudan's Kordofan region and an army stronghold.

places.name: Al-Khuway
places.why: Town in West Kordofan on the road towards Darfur.
places.ref_note: Only OpenStreetMap has a coordinate for this place, so it has one reference.

places.name: El Fasher
places.why: Main city of North Darfur in western Sudan.

places.name: Addis Ababa
places.why: Capital of Ethiopia, Africa's second most populous country.

places.name: Mekelle
places.why: Capital of Ethiopia's northern Tigray region. A TPLF-led alliance briefly held it until 3 October 2026; government-allied forces then took it.

places.name: Asmara
places.why: Capital of Eritrea, Ethiopia's northern neighbour on the Red Sea.

places.name: Zalambessa
places.why: Ethiopian town right on the border with Eritrea.

places.name: Bamako
places.why: Capital of Mali, ruled by the army since coups in 2020 and 2021.

places.name: Kidal
places.why: Desert town in northern Mali, long a base of Tuareg rebels. Mali's army says it retook it on 6 October 2026.

places.name: Rudnik nad Sanem
places.why: Town in southeast Poland near where Russian missiles fell on 20 November 2026.

places.name: Berlin
places.why: Capital of Germany.

events.title: US blockade and Hormuz shipping standoff continue
summary: The US blockade of Iranian ports continues, and Iran still restricts the Strait of Hormuz.
UKMTO counted six ship strikes in the week to 20 November, and more tanker hits on 21 November.
Iran says mines hit tankers. UKMTO has not confirmed mines.
events.why_it_matters: About one fifth of world oil normally passed the strait, so the standoff affects energy prices and shipping worldwide.
events.verify_note: Iran's mine claims and the JMIC count of seven tankers hit since 16 November (reported by Iran International) were not confirmed by UKMTO. Latest weekly transit count was not found.

sources.title: Trump threatens Iran strikes in new year, says blockade runners will be sunk
sources.supports: Trump says he leans toward strikes after the new year and that blockade runners would be sunk. Iran claims mine hits on tankers; UKMTO has not confirmed.

sources.title: Bahrain says Iranian attack causes fire at industrial facility
sources.supports: Guards say they hit US sites in Bahrain; Bahrain reports a fire at a civilian facility. A Qatari delegation held talks in Tehran. Tankers reportedly hit in Hormuz.

sources.title: Reports Claim Iran Is Preparing Oil Convoy to Test U.S. Blockade
sources.supports: Fars claims 14 tankers ready at Kharg; TankerTrackers doubts it. Kpler data cited by Reuters show no Iranian crude loadings in October. UKMTO logged six strikes in seven days.

sources.title: Live Updates: Trump says he wants "permanent" deal with Iran; warns next move may not come until 2027
sources.supports: Timeline 17 to 22 November: US strike on Qeshm, Bahrain attacks, tankers hit 20 and 21 November, Trump not rushing, Iran ties nuclear talk to lifting the blockade.

events.title: How the US-Iran war reached today's standoff
summary: The US and Israel struck Iran on 28 February 2026. Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei was killed.
A Pakistan-brokered ceasefire began in April. A June memorandum promised an end to fighting and talks toward a final deal.
Fighting resumed in July after ship attacks. Now there is neither full war nor peace.
events.why_it_matters: Every current question, from the blockade to the nuclear stock, comes from the war that began on 28 February and its failed deals.
events.verify_note: Sources differ by a day or so on some dates: ceasefire 7 or 8 April, memorandum announced 14 June and called the 17 June memorandum elsewhere. Signing was planned for 19 June, per France 24.

sources.title: US-Iran war, then and now: How the landscape has changed since February
sources.supports: Strikes began 28 February during nuclear talks. Khamenei was killed and his son Mojtaba succeeded him. Brent rose from $72 to a peak above $126.

sources.title: Pakistan army chief in Tehran: Can diplomacy prevent new US-Iran fighting?
sources.supports: Pakistan brokered the 8 April ceasefire. A 14-point June memorandum followed. Its 60-day window expired mid-August. Trump rejected an Iranian proposal on 26 September.

sources.title: March to July: What's different as US-Iran fighting escalates again?
sources.supports: Iran struck three vessels on 6 July and the US replied the next day. Trump called the ceasefire over and Iran shut the strait again.

sources.title: US and Iran agree to 'immediate' end of military operations in memorandum of understanding
sources.supports: Pakistan announced the memorandum on 14 June. It promised to reopen the strait, end the blockade, and start nuclear talks within about two months.

sources.title: Iran leader Khamenei killed in massive US and Israeli attack
sources.supports: Khamenei was killed in the opening wave of a large US and Israeli attack on 28 February. Iran fired at Israel and US Gulf bases.

sources.title: US-Iran ceasefire deal: What are the terms, and what's next?
sources.supports: A two-week Pakistan-brokered ceasefire followed about 40 days of US-Israeli attacks.

events.title: Small strikes and drone attacks keep flaring
summary: A US official says jets hit a Guards missile site on Qeshm Island on 17 November.
The Guards say they hit US radars at two Bahrain bases on 21 November.
A US official says no US forces were damaged. Bahrain rejects the Guards' account; injury reports differ.
events.why_it_matters: Attacks on a Gulf state hosting the US Fifth Fleet raise the risk that the limited exchanges widen into renewed war.
events.verify_note: Disputed: the Guards claim hits on US radars; a US official says there was no US damage. Bahrain's Interior Ministry reports no injuries; its Foreign Ministry reports two, per Iran International. CENTCOM denied a new Qeshm strike on 20 November.

sources.title: Bahrain says Iranian attack causes fire at industrial facility
sources.supports: Guards say they hit US sites in Bahrain; Bahrain reports a fire at a civilian facility. A Qatari delegation held talks in Tehran. Tankers reportedly hit in Hormuz.

sources.title: Trump threatens Iran strikes in new year, says blockade runners will be sunk
sources.supports: Trump says he leans toward strikes after the new year and that blockade runners would be sunk. Iran claims mine hits on tankers; UKMTO has not confirmed.

sources.title: Live Updates: Trump says he wants "permanent" deal with Iran; warns next move may not come until 2027
sources.supports: Timeline 17 to 22 November: US strike on Qeshm, Bahrain attacks, tankers hit 20 and 21 November, Trump not rushing, Iran ties nuclear talk to lifting the blockade.

sources.title: US jets strike IRGC missile launch site on Iran's Qeshm Island in self-defence
sources.supports: A US official says jets hit a Guards missile site on Qeshm on 17 November in self-defence, after Iran's third attack on Bahrain in under a week.

events.title: Iran's uranium stock unchecked as IAEA is blocked
summary: At the IAEA board around 19 November, four Western powers urged Iran to let inspectors back in.
IAEA chief Grossi said only the undamaged Bushehr plant was inspected last quarter.
Iran has not said where its enriched uranium is. It asks whether the demand serves a new attack.
events.why_it_matters: Without inspections nobody can verify whether Iran is rebuilding a weapons-capable programme, which is the US core demand.
events.verify_note: The 19 November IAEA board pressure rests on one Reuters report, carried by Al-Monitor. The 440 kg figure is the IAEA's pre-June-2025 estimate. A second outlet on the board meeting was not found.

sources.title: West presses Iran, IAEA let inspections resume at bombed nuclear sites
sources.supports: At the IAEA board the US, UK, France and Germany urged access. Grossi said only Bushehr was inspected last quarter. Iran questions the aim of the demand.

sources.title: Live Updates: Trump says he wants "permanent" deal with Iran; warns next move may not come until 2027
sources.supports: Timeline 17 to 22 November: US strike on Qeshm, Bahrain attacks, tankers hit 20 and 21 November, Trump not rushing, Iran ties nuclear talk to lifting the blockade.

events.title: Iran's oil exports halted by blockade
summary: Kpler says Iran loaded no crude in September or October. Reuters carried the data.
Kpler counts about 20 loaded tankers idle near Kharg Island, holding 43 million barrels. Windward counts more.
Iranian state-linked media hint tankers may try to run the blockade. Trump says runners would be sunk.
events.why_it_matters: Iran lost about 200 to 250 million dollars a day in oil revenue, Kpler estimates. That pressure explains talk of testing the blockade.
events.verify_note: Trackers differ: Bloomberg dated the Kharg halt to late August; Kpler reports no loadings in September or October. Kpler counts about 20 loaded tankers, Windward 31. A tanker run is unconfirmed: Fars says 14 are ready; TankerTrackers doubts it.

sources.title: Trump threatens Iran strikes in new year, says blockade runners will be sunk
sources.supports: Trump says he leans toward strikes after the new year and that blockade runners would be sunk. Iran claims mine hits on tankers; UKMTO has not confirmed.

sources.title: With Oil Revenue Running Out, Iran Teases Breaking US Blockade
sources.supports: Kpler sees about 20 loaded tankers idle near Kharg, 43 million barrels stuck inside the blockade, and export revenue possibly hitting zero by mid December.

sources.title: Reports Claim Iran Is Preparing Oil Convoy to Test U.S. Blockade
sources.supports: Fars claims 14 tankers ready at Kharg; TankerTrackers doubts it. Kpler data cited by Reuters show no Iranian crude loadings in October. UKMTO logged six strikes in seven days.

sources.title: Iran readies tankers to run US blockade, threatens Persian Gulf oil if fired on
sources.supports: Iranian state-linked media signal tankers may test the blockade. Fars threatens Gulf oil facilities if ships are fired on. No Iranian official confirmed a convoy.

sources.title: Iran's main oil terminals remain empty as US blockade bites
sources.supports: Bloomberg reported no tankers docked at Kharg crude terminals since late August.

events.title: Mediated talks stall as Trump cools on a deal
summary: A Qatari delegation held about two hours of talks in Tehran on 20 November, Iran says.
Araghchi says discussing Hormuz's reopening is pointless until Iran's demands are met, state TV reported.
Trump says he is not rushing and wants a permanent deal. He leans toward strikes after New Year.
events.why_it_matters: With talks stuck, the blockade and Hormuz restrictions stay in place and renewed strikes remain possible.
events.verify_note: Iran gave no details of the Qatari talks. Trump's remarks on timing vary between interviews. CBS cites sources saying the US and Israel weigh a new assault; not confirmed officially.

sources.supports: Guards say they hit US sites in Bahrain; Bahrain reports a fire at a civilian facility. A Qatari delegation held talks in Tehran. Tankers reportedly hit in Hormuz.

events.hotspot: Yemen, Saudi Arabia and the Red Sea
events.title: Houthis launch near daily strikes on Saudi Arabia
summary: Since 7 November the Houthis say they attack Saudi Arabia almost daily, hitting oil sites, airports and bases.
Saudi officials report shrapnel damage to an Aramco building in Riyadh and a fire on the East-West pipeline.
On 22 November the Saudi-led coalition said it shot down more Houthi drones, Anadolu reported.
events.why_it_matters: Saudi oil exports and Red Sea shipping are exposed while the Strait of Hormuz is already disrupted.
events.verify_note: The 22 November intercepts rest on one Anadolu report (22 November). Near daily attacks since 7 November are reported by Al Jazeera and the Long War Journal, run by the FDD think tank. Saudi Arabia reports only shrapnel damage to an Aramco building and a pipeline fire.

sources.title: Saudi-led coalition intercepts Houthi drone targeting southern Saudi Arabia
sources.supports: The coalition said on X that it destroyed a Houthi drone launched toward southern Saudi Arabia, after downing another aimed at the Riyadh region. No location or damage given.

sources.title: Houthis sustain missile and drone attacks across Saudi Arabia
sources.supports: Day by day log from 7 to 14 November: Houthi claims on Riyadh, Yanbu and pipeline sites; Saudi confirms an Aramco building hit and a pipeline fire; coalition reports intercepts.

sources.title: Yemen's Houthis renew strikes on Saudi Arabia as UNSC extends sanctions
sources.supports: Houthis claim new strikes on Saudi oil and air sites; coalition reports intercepts; UN Security Council extends Yemen sanctions.

sources.title: Is Syria sending 600 troops to help Saudi Arabia fight Houthis? Damascus denies Yemen deployment
sources.supports: Saudi authorities warned Riyadh residents of a hostile aerial threat on 9 November. Houthis claim Saudi strikes killed 44 people; unverified.

events.title: Israeli tanks raid central Gaza as truce strains
summary: Reuters says Israeli tanks raided central Gaza on 18 November, the first ground raid since the October 2025 truce.
Gaza's health ministry says 1,661 people were killed since the truce began, nine in two days of strikes.
The US-backed Board of Peace warned the truce could collapse and may hand reconstruction to the UN.
events.why_it_matters: If the truce collapses, displaced families in Gaza face renewed war while flooding already hits their tent shelters.
events.verify_note: Death tolls come from Gaza's health ministry and cannot be independently checked. Israel says its strikes target Hamas regrouping; Hamas calls the raid a violation. The Board of Peace adviser's remarks were made to Israeli outlet Ynet, read through The National.

sources.title: Displaced Palestinians protest as Israeli air strikes continue in Gaza
sources.supports: Ministry counts 1,661 killed since the truce; nearly two thirds of Gaza under Israeli control or restriction; over 500 homes razed in under a month, per a local mayor.

sources.title: Strikes kill nine in Gaza as Board of Peace adviser criticises Israel
sources.supports: Nine killed in two days; Board of Peace says the truce risks collapse and its adviser says it will hand the keys to the UN if Israel keeps obstructing reconstruction.

sources.title: Gaza ceasefire: Israeli tanks advance in Gaza to target Hamas
sources.supports: Israeli tanks entered central Gaza, the first ground operation since the truce; Israel says Hamas is rearming; Hamas calls it a dangerous escalation.

events.title: Israel and Lebanon split over force replacing UNIFIL
summary: Israel's UN envoy said on 17 November that Israel will rely only on its own troops at the border.
On 20 November US envoy Mike Waltz said Washington is asking several countries for a disarmament verification force.
The UN force's mandate ends on 31 December. Lebanon wants a replacement; Hezbollah rejects disarming.
events.why_it_matters: Without agreement on who verifies disarmament, a security gap could open in south Lebanon when UNIFIL leaves.
events.verify_note: A claim that the US and Israel favour private contractors comes only from Antiwar.com, an advocacy outlet, and is left out. Israeli think-tank reporting that Lebanon sees no point in another talks round before Israel's government forms was not opened directly.

sources.title: US in talks with several countries on force to verify Hezbollah disarmament in Lebanon, says envoy
sources.supports: Waltz says verification force is under active discussion; UN Security Council statement backs UNIFIL and discusses withdrawal; Lebanon and Israel disagree on who verifies.

sources.title: Israel repeats rejection of peacekeepers on Lebanon border as Unifil withdrawal looms
sources.supports: Israel's UN envoy Danon says Israel trusts only its own soldiers; Lebanon asked the Council to reconsider ending UNIFIL and seeks a multinational force.

sources.title: Israel Strikes East Lebanon, Says Targeting Hezbollah Arms
sources.supports: Israel struck the Anti-Lebanon mountains saying it hit an arms shipment; Lebanese authorities have a disarmament plan Hezbollah rejects.

sources.title: Lebanon, November 2026 Monthly Forecast
sources.supports: Israeli forces hold semi-permanent positions in the south; talks in Florida in October had no breakthrough; UNIFIL's mandate ends 31 December 2026.

events.title: Iraqi forces enter Kataib Hezbollah stronghold under deal
summary: After a negotiated deal, Iraqi forces began entering Jurf al-Sakhar on 20 November, Iraqi officials say.
Kataib Hezbollah brigades are being replaced under a joint command. Some fighters still held ground on 21 November.
The PM's office says this could bring forward the June 2027 deadline for state control of weapons.
events.why_it_matters: It tests whether Iraq's state can take control of an area long held by an armed group.
events.verify_note: The entry itself rests on one 964media report (22 November), which dates it to Friday 20 November and says fighters were still present on 21 November. Reuters and Al Jazeera reported the deal before entry. Full withdrawal is not confirmed.

sources.title: Jurf al-Sakhar could bring Iraq's arms deadline forward, spokesperson says
sources.supports: Forces began entering on 21 November under a Federal Police led command; three Kataib Hezbollah brigades are being replaced; fighters remained on one side on 21 November.

sources.title: Iraqi forces to enter Kataib Hezbollah stronghold in Jurf al-Nasr on Nov 20
sources.supports: Forces were due to deploy on 20 November under a deal by senior Shiite figures; Kataib Hezbollah to be redeployed; Qaani in Baghdad.

sources.title: What is Iraq's Jurf al-Sakhar and what is behind gov't push to control it?
sources.supports: Qaani and al-Zaidi reportedly reached a tentative deal for Kataib Hezbollah to withdraw; the group denies smuggling and calls the push extortion.

sources.title: Iraq vows to 'cleanse' militia stronghold Jurf Al Sakhar of oil smuggling
sources.supports: Ruling alliance split over entering the area; troops massed outside; 20 November deadline; phased handover seen as most likely outcome.

events.title: Syria's role in Saudi defence disputed after deal
summary: AP reports Syrian advisers are in Saudi Arabia and about 600 special forces are due to arrive.
Syria's foreign minister says there is no deployment to Yemen and none planned soon.
AFP, citing Yemeni sources, reports Syrians already in Yemen. Syria denies it.
events.why_it_matters: Syria's new government is tying itself to Saudi Arabia as Houthi attacks on the kingdom grow.
events.verify_note: AP, AFP and Syria's government give conflicting accounts of what Syrian forces are doing. The 600 figure rests on anonymous officials, and AFP's higher numbers on Yemeni sources are unverified. No reporting after 9 November was found.

sources.title: Syria confirms sending troops to Saudi Arabia amid battle against Houthis
sources.supports: Syrian officials told AP advisers are in Saudi Arabia and 600 special forces are due; a Syrian official says the role is training, and denies fighting in Yemen.

sources.title: Is Syria sending 600 troops to help Saudi Arabia fight Houthis? Damascus denies Yemen deployment
sources.supports: Foreign Minister al-Shaibani says no troops are going to Yemen; AP cites officials on 600 special forces; AFP cites Yemeni sources claiming Syrians already in Yemen.

sources.title: Syria, Saudi Arabia sign defence cooperation deal, agree $403m in loans
sources.supports: Defence ministries signed an agreement with undisclosed terms; six Saudi loans worth over $403m.

events.title: Ukraine cripples Kerch bridge; Russia launches huge retaliation
summary: Ukraine hit the Kerch bridge on 16 to 19 November. Reuters verified images of a destroyed road section.
Zelensky says Russia fired over 400 drones and 110 missiles on 20 November, killing at least eight civilians.
A Berlin summit on 19 November prepared a four-way next round including Europe. Land talks have no breakthrough.
events.why_it_matters: Damage to the Crimea bridge makes supplying Crimea harder for Russia, Reuters says, while talks stay stuck on territory.
events.verify_note: Bridge damage claims come from officials on both sides; Reuters verified images of the road span. Russia says no one was hurt in the latest bridge attack; Crimea's Russian-installed governor says two died. Missile and drone counts are Zelensky's.

sources.title: Russian missiles hit Poland: What happened, and could NATO respond?
sources.supports: Zelensky says Russia fired over 400 drones and at least 110 missiles overnight, killing at least eight; the strike followed Putin's vow to retaliate for the Kerch bridge attacks.

sources.title: Strikes on Kerch Bridge can force Kremlin to reconsider its position on negotiations, Ukraine at OSCE
sources.supports: Timeline of bridge attacks 16 to 19 November; Ukraine's General Staff says Neptune missiles hit the rail tracks and Russia suspended trains.

sources.title: Ukraine strikes Putin's prized Crimean bridge for third time in a week
